CITY OF CABOT, ARKANSAS
Council Meeting Minutes
May 18, 2020

In response to the 2020 COVID-19 Pandemic and restrictions placed on
social distancing by the Centers for Disease Control, the City of Cabot
moved the monthly Council Meeting to the Veterans Park Event Center, 508
N. Lincoln, as advertised. This allowed for spacing between chairs, as
suggested. The meeting was both open to the public and an online meeting
with video through the web-based video conferencing tool Zoom. The event
was successfully streamed through YouTube.

Mayor Ken Kincade called to order the regular meeting of the Cabot City
Council at 7:01 p.m. on May 18, 2020 in the Veterans Park Event Center.
The opening prayer was given and the Pledge of Allegiance was led by
Mayor Kincade.

Roll Call

A roll call was conducted. The following Council Members were present:
Ronald Waymack and Doug Warner attended the meeting in person. Council
Members Damon Bivins, Norma Naquin, James Reid, Matt Webber, and Ed
Long all attended the meeting via Zoom. Kevin Davis was absent. Also in
attendance were City Attorney Ben Hooper (via Zoom), City Clerk &
Treasurer Tammy Yocom, and IT Director Roger Self. Several members of
the public were also in attendance.

ORDINANCE NO. 17 OF 2020
AN ORDINANCE CREATING AND CERTIFYING TAX LIENS AGAINST REAL
PROPERTIES AT VARIOUS LOCATIONS WITHIN THE CITY OF CABOT FOR
FUNDS EXPENDED TO PAY FOR SERVICES RENDERED DUE TO CODE
VIOLATIONS; DECLARING AN EMERGENCY; AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
WHEREAS, due to violations of the City of Cabot, Arkansas Code of Ordinances, the
City of Cabot has expended funds for services rendered and/or performed by and/or on behalf of
the City of Cabot for certain work on real properties located within the city limits to
remove/modify various noncompliant conditions. A list of said real properties is attached hereto
as Exhibit “A.”

WHEREAS, despite notice and demand, said property owners have not paid the amounts
due to the city for services rendered and/or performed as detailed herein; and

WHEREAS, pursuant to Arkansas law, tax liens should be created and certified for these
real properties and record property owners listed above. Further, the lien amounts should be
certified for inclusion in the annual real estate tax statements prepared by the Lonoke County
Treasurer’s Office.

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF CABOT,
ARKANSAS, THAT:

SECTION 1: In accordance with the authority granted under A.C.A. §14-54-904, the
Cabot City Council hereby authorizes the Mayor and/or the City Clerk to certify the list of real
properties and amounts due, plus ten percent (10%), included herein to the Lonoke County
Treasurer’s Office for inclusion as tax liens on the annual real property tax statements for 2019.
A list of said real properties is attached hereto as Exhibit “A”, is attached hereto and
incorporated herein by this reference.

SECTION 2: Emergency Clause. Due to the statutory timeframes to file liens, it is in the
best interest, welfare and safety of the citizens of the City of Cabot and an emergency is hereby
declared to exist and this Ordinance shall be in full force and effect immediately upon and after

its passage by the Council.

Cabot City Council Work Session
Veterans Park Event Center
June 1, 2020
6:30 p.m.

In response to the 2020 COVID-19 Pandemic and restrictions placed on social distancing
by the Centers for Disease Control, the City of Cabot moved the monthly Work Session
to the Veterans Park Event Center, 508 N. Lincoln, as advertised. This allowed for ten
feet of spacing between chairs, as suggested. The meeting was both open to the public
and an online meeting with video through the web-based video conferencing tool Zoom.
The event was successfully streamed through YouTube.

Council members present via Zoom were: Ed Long, James Reid, Kevin Davis, Norma
Naquin and Matt Webber. Doug Warner and Ron Waymack attended the meeting in
person. Damon Bivins was absent. Others present: Mayor Ken Kincade, City Attorney
Ben Hooper (via Zoom), City Clerk & Treasurer Tammy Yocom, and Roger Self, IT
Director.

Municipal Services Committee Business: (Members are: Long, Reid & Webber)

As Chairman, Ed Long, opened with discussion on extending the current trash
contract with Waste Connections, Inc. or rebidding the service. Mr. Kendrick Ketchum,
representing Waste Connections, Inc., addressed the council answering questions and
responding to numerous concerns of the council. Mr. Stubby Stumbaugh, representing
Waste Corporation of Arkansas (WCA), addressed the council explaining their desire for
a rebid, calling it a “premium contract”. Should the City award WCA the bid, they can be
ready in 90 days. Discussion. It was determined the council would like to: vote on
extending the current contract through January 1, 2021 during the June 2020 Council
Meeting; vote on a resolution to put the service out for bid during the June 2020 Council
Meeting; and award the bid during the August 2020 Council Meeting, provided it can be
sought in July and be ready for a vote. No action by vote.

Budget & Personnel Committee Business: (Members are: Warner, Webber &
Naquin)

Mayor Kincade reported city and county sales tax combined for May (March sales)
is up $100,000 from May 2019. He thanked the citizens for taking care of Cabot and
encouraged all to visit local businesses. Mayor Kincade will continue to monitor the
expenditures and revenue as we wait on June numbers. Discussion. As Chairman, Doug
Warner, agreed the City is looking good financially. No action by vote.

Police & Fire Committee Business: (Members are: Bivins, Waymack and Long)
Chairman, Damon Bivins was absent. No action by vote.

Community Development Committee Business: (Members are: Davis, Bivins and
Naquin)

--- page 2 (OCR) ---
As Chairman, Kevin Davis, stated there was nothing on the agenda for tonight. He
reminded all that Amy Williams, President/CEO Cabot Chamber of Commerce, will provide
the 2020 Q2 report next month via email. Amy announced exciting news is coming up.
She hopes to be able to share it soon. No action by vote.

Military Affairs Committee Business: (Members are: Waymack, Warner, Reid)
As Chairman, Ron Waymack, stated there was nothing on the agenda for tonight.
No action by vote.

Council Member, Matt Webber, asked is it was possible to require the Chairmen of all City
commissions to provide a report to the council. Discussion. It was agreed upon that it
was necessary and could be done. Ed Long agreed to ask the A&P Commission Chairman

MEMORANDUM OF UNDERTSANDING
This document is a memorandum of understanding that reflects and agreement between
the City of Cabot (the City), the Cabot Foundation for Arts & Culture (CFAC), and Glenda Krauss
(Krauss):
1. The City is the owner of the old Firehouse building located at 114 West Pine Street in
Cabot, Arkansas. CFAC is a nonprofit organization whose mission is to encourage and
promote community through the advancement of art and culture in Cabot. Glenda
Krauss is an artist who has been selected through a public art initiative administered by
CFAC to paint a mural on the east wall of the old Firehouse building located at 114 West
Pine Street. This Memorandum documents the agreement between all these parties in
regards to the commissioned mural.
2. CFAC’s purpose behind the initiative is to encourage artistic expression and foster a
greater appreciation for art in the Cabot community. CFAC is dedicated to present
public art that enhances Cabot’s imaginative capacity, enlivens the neighborhoods,
contributes to economic vitality, sparks civic exchange, and enhances community
connection.
3. Krauss and CFAC agree that mural will be painted and installed to appear substantially
identical to the design that was approved by the Cabot City Council. Installation will be
completed by June 30, 2020.
4. The entirety of the mural will be paid for by CFAC. The estimated cost is $7,500 for the
mural and $1,000 for UV protectant/anti-graffiti coating. It is agreed that CFAC will
have full ownership of the commissioned mural. The City maintains full ownership of the
building and the wall on which the mural will be displayed. CFAC will have all rights to
marketing, both commercial and noncommercial, associated with the mural as well as
general commercial rights. The City shall have the right to use photographic images of
the mural in tourism and municipal promotion. The City may exercise that right
noncommercially via such mediums as social media posts, website postings, promotional
messages, and other related methods.
5. The City agrees to keep to the completed mural illuminated at night.
6. The City agrees that it will not paint over the mural for a period of 20 years. CFAC
likewise agrees that it will maintain the mural in good aesthetic condition for 20 years.
The City not painting over the wall for 20 years is specifically conditioned on CFAC
maintaining the good aesthetic condition of the mural for the same period of time. The
20-year period referenced here may be extended or shortened by written agreement
between CFAC and the City. The parties recognize that the Cabot City Council has the
authority to sell the building at issue and that the agreement to display and maintain the
mural for 20 years will terminate if the building is sold.
7. Krauss has secured an insurance policy in regards to the installation and early display
and use of the mural for the City’s benefit and agrees not to cancel or otherwise

68

undermine that policy prior to its expiration. CFAC agrees to indemnify they City and
hold it blameless for any injury or any other claims or causes of action that arise out of
the installation, use, or display of the mural. The parties also agree that the City will not
be liable for any damages caused to the mural as a result of fire, accident, structural
damage, vandalism, act of God, or any similar cause.

I acknowledge that I have fully read, fully understand, and fully agree with all of the above

MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING
This document is a memorandum of understanding that reflects an agreement between the City of
Cabot (the City), The Cabot Chamber of Commerce (The Chamber), White County Medical Center
d/b/a Unity Health – White County Medical Center (“Unity Health”), and White Artworks (White)
1. The City is the owner of the building located at 1 City Plaza in Cabot, Arkansas. The
Chamber is a nonprofit organization whose mission is to advance the commercial,
financial, industrial, and civic interest in Cabot and the surrounding areas. Unity Health is
a nonprofit Hospital that has partnered with the Chamber to commission a mural on the
eastern wall of 1 City Plaza. Jason White of White Artworks is the artist who has been
selected by the Chamber and Unity Health to install the mural. This Memorandum
documents the agreement between all these parties regarding the commissioned mural.
2. All parties involved agree that the purpose behind this initiative is to encourage artistic
expression, bring light to community connection, and foster a greater appreciation for art
in the Cabot community. The parties are dedicated to present public art that enhances
Cabot’s imaginative capacity, enliven the neighborhoods, contribute to economic vitality,
spark civic exchange, and strengthen community connection.
3. The parties agree that White will begin work on the mural on approximately August 1st,
2020, and the estimated completion date will be August 20th, 2020.
4. The entire cost of the mural will be paid by Unity Health. The estimated cost is $5,000 for
the mural. It is agreed that Unity Health will have full ownership of the commissioned
mural. The City maintains full ownership of the building and the wall on which the mural
will be displayed. Unity Health will have all rights to marketing the mural, both
commercial and noncommercial, as well as general commercial rights to the mural. The
City and Cabot Chamber of Commerce shall have the right to use photographic images of
the mural in tourism promotion and municipal promotion. The City and the Cabot Chamber
of Commerce may exercise such rights non-commercially via such mediums as social
media posts, website postings, promotional messages, and other related methods.
5. The City agrees to keep the completed mural illuminated at night.
6. The City agrees that it will not paint over the mural for ten years. Unity Health and White
Artworks likewise agrees that it will maintain the mural in a good aesthetic condition for
ten years. The obligation of the City to not paint over the mural for ten years is specifically
conditioned on Unity Health and White Artworks maintaining the good aesthetic condition
of the mural for the same period. The ten year period referenced here may be extended or
shortened only by written agreement of Unity Health and the City. The parties recognize
that the Cabot City Council maintains the authority to sell this building and that the

RESOLUTION NO. 27 OF 2020

CITY OF CABOT, ARKASNAS IS ESSENTIAL: IN SUPPORT OF FAIR, DIRECT
FEDERAL EMERGENCY SUPPORT TO REOPEN AND REBUILD LOCAL
AMERICAN ECONOMIES

WHEREAS, America’s cities, towns and villages face unprecedented threats due to the
ongoing COVID-19 pandemic emergency; and

WHEREAS, municipalities are essential to America’s economic recovery and without
funding support for local governments, municipalities may go from being a critical part of the
economic solution, to becoming a major obstacle to long-term stabilization and recovery; and

WHEREAS, America’s cities, towns and villages will experience budgetary shortfalls in
fiscal year 2020 alone, and the negative effects of the pandemic emergency on local communities
will continue long after this year; and

WHEREAS, three million critical municipal worker jobs are at risk, threatening cuts to
basic community services, including 9-1-1 response, sanitation, and maintenance; and

WHEREAS, communities have taken extraordinary measures to protect health, safety, and
the continuation of essential services throughout the emergency; and

WHEREAS, America’s rural communities and small towns are struggling just as much as
big cities and risk being left behind or wiped out entirely.

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED THAT THE CITY OF CABOT,
ARKANSAS CALLS ON CONGRESS TO ALLOCATE FAIR AND DIRECT FEDERAL
SUPPORT TO ALL OF AMERICA’S COMMUNITIES, REGARDLESS OF
POPULATION SIZE; AND

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that this funding must be flexible and address not only the
additional expenses incurred by communities to respond to the pandemic emergency, but also the
dramatic budgetary shortfalls resulting from pauses in commerce, tourism, other economic
engines; and

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that local governments will ensure federal funds are
immediately used to rebuild and reopen the national economy; and

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that funding will keep middle class workers employed and
critical services operating; and

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED THAT the City of Cabot, Arkasnas has been part of the
emergency response and now calls on Congress to build a united national partnership for a safe,
healthy, prosperous life.

reported when collected. The effect on the financial statements of this departure from the regulatory basis has not been
determined.

A RESOLUTION DECLARING THE STRUCTURE LOCATED AT 1100
WEST ELM STREET IN THE CITY OF CABOT TO CONSTITUTE A
PUBLIC NUISANCE AND CONDEMNING SAID STRUCTURES;
PROVIDING A PERIOD OF TIME FOR PROPERTY OWNERS TO ABATE
SAID NUISANCE; AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
WHEREAS, the buildings and structures whose location is set forth herein are
vacant and have become run down, dilapidated, unsightly, dangerous, obnoxious, unsafe,
not fit for human habitation and detrimental to the public welfare of citizens and residents;
and
WHEREAS, the condition of such property constitutes a serious fire and health
hazard to the City of Cabot, and unless immediate actions are taken to remedy this
situation by removing, razing and abating said nuisance, there is a great likelihood that
the surrounding property may be destroyed by fire originating from such unsafe and
hazardous structures, and also that since structures are without proper sanitary facilities
and as such are unsafe and hazardous and a breeding place for rats, rodents and other
dangerous germ carriers of diseases, such buildings constitute a serious hazard to the
health and safety of the citizens of Cabot, and they should be moved or razed for the
purpose of eliminating such hazards.
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF
THE CITY OF CABOT ARKANSAS:
SECTION 1: That the City Council hereby declares the buildings, houses and
other structures located at the property identified in Section 2 below to be vacant and run
down, dilapidated, unsafe, unsightly, dangerous, obnoxious, unsanitary, a fire hazard, a
menace to abutting properties, with the current condition of said structures not being fit
for human habitation; and because of such conditions, the City Council declares the same
to be condemned as a public nuisance and is ordered abated, removed or razed by the
owners thereof.
SECTION 2: That the owners of record of 1100 West Elm Street, Cabot
Arkansas, 72023 are hereby directed to raze the same or otherwise abate the said nuisance

within thirty (30) days after the posting of a true copy of this Resolution at a conspicuous
place upon the structure constituting the nuisance.
SECTION 3: If the aforementioned structures have not been razed and/or
removed within thirty (30) days after posting a true copy of this Resolution at a
conspicuous place upon the structures constituting the nuisance, or the nuisance otherwise
abated, the structures shall be torn down and/or removed by the Mayor or his duly
designated representative. Each day after the aforesaid thirty (30) days in which said
nuisance is not abated may be punishable by a fine or sanction provided by law.
SECTION 4: That the provisions of this Resolution are hereby declared to be
severable and if any section, phrase or provision shall be declared or held invalid, such
invalidity shall not affect the remainder of the sections, phrases or provisions.
SECTION 5: That this Resolution shall be in full force and effect from and after
its passage and approval.

MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING
This document is a memorandum of understanding that reflects an agreement between the City of
Cabot (the City), The Cabot Chamber of Commerce (The Chamber), White County Medical Center
d/b/a Unity Health – White County Medical Center (“Unity Health”), and White Artworks (White)
1. The City is the owner of the building located at 1 City Plaza in Cabot, Arkansas. The
Chamber is a nonprofit organization whose mission is to advance the commercial,
financial, industrial, and civic interest in Cabot and the surrounding areas. Unity Health is
a nonprofit Hospital that has partnered with the Chamber to commission a mural on the
eastern wall of 1 City Plaza. Jason White of White Artworks is the artist who has been
selected by the Chamber and Unity Health to install the mural. This Memorandum
documents the agreement between all these parties regarding the commissioned mural.
2. All parties involved agree that the purpose behind this initiative is to encourage artistic
expression, bring light to community connection, and foster a greater appreciation for art
in the Cabot community. The parties are dedicated to present public art that enhances
Cabot’s imaginative capacity, enliven the neighborhoods, contribute to economic vitality,
spark civic exchange, and strengthen community connection.
3. The parties agree that White will begin work on the mural on approximately August 1st,
2020, and the estimated completion date will be August 20th, 2020.
4. The entire cost of the mural will be paid by Unity Health. The estimated cost is $5,000 for
the mural. It is agreed that Unity Health will have full ownership of the commissioned
mural. The City maintains full ownership of the building and the wall on which the mural
will be displayed. Unity Health will have all rights to marketing the mural, both
commercial and noncommercial, as well as general commercial rights to the mural. The
City and Cabot Chamber of Commerce shall have the right to use photographic images of
the mural in tourism promotion and municipal promotion. The City and the Cabot Chamber
of Commerce may exercise such rights non-commercially via such mediums as social
media posts, website postings, promotional messages, and other related methods.
5. The City agrees to keep the completed mural illuminated at night.
6. The City agrees that it will not paint over the mural for ten years. Unity Health and White
Artworks likewise agrees that it will maintain the mural in a good aesthetic condition for
ten years. The obligation of the City to not paint over the mural for ten years is specifically
conditioned on Unity Health and White Artworks maintaining the good aesthetic condition
of the mural for the same period. The ten year period referenced here may be extended or
shortened only by written agreement of Unity Health and the City. The parties recognize
that the Cabot City Council maintains the authority to sell this building and that the

12

agreement to display and maintain the mural for ten years will terminate if the building is
sold.
7. White agrees to maintain adequate liability insurance and agrees to provide proof of such
insurance to Unity Health, the City and the Chamber prior to beginning any work on the
mural. White further agrees to indemnify and hold harmless, Unity Health, the City, and
the Chamber, from and against any liability for any damage or injury suffered while
working on the mural.
8. The Chamber and Unity Health agree to indemnify the City and hold it harmless for any
injury or any other claims or causes of action that arise out of the installation, use, or display
of the mural. The parties also agree that the City will not be liable for any damages caused
to the mural because of fire, accident, structural damage, vandalism, act of God, or any
similar cause.
The parties acknowledge that they each have fully read, fully understand, and fully agree with all
of the above provisions.

A Fire Pension Board Meeting was held on Tuesday, February 18, 2020 at 10:00 a.m. in the conference
room at City Hall. Members present were: Carl Pickard, Jimmie Bell, and William (Bill) Clark. All others
were absent. Others present were: Mayor, Ken Kincade, City Attorney, Ben Hooper, City Clerk &
Treasurer, Tammy Yocom and Deputy Clerk, Lisa Milam.

1. Mayor, Ken Kincade called the meeting to order at 10:03.

Handouts were as follows, a copy of the Memo on Consolidation of Local Plan for year 2020 from the
Arkansas Fire & Police Pension Review Board, a voting ballet and an information update form to all
present.

2. Discussion regarding voting on board member’s ensued. Followed with a vote by ballot from all
present board members, the Mayor and Tammy. The vote was unanimous for all 5 members
residing within the state of Arkansas to serve on the board. Vote 5 — 0 in favor.

3. Discussion regarding voting on a 3% raise for 2020 retroactive to 1/01/2020. Motion to adopt, by
Jimmie Bell. Second by Carl Pickard. Vote 5 —O all in favor.

4. Discussion regarding consolidation with LOPFI. Carl Pickard asked about the amount of monies in
the Fire Pension Fund at present. Tammy handed out a Stephen’s statement confirming the
account balance as $3,018, 065.92 in the Fire Pension Relief Fund as of Dec. 31, 2019. Carl stated
that “The board has so few members now that it is hard to even get a quorum together, so if it is
all the same | feel like we should consolidate.” Carl then: motioned to consolidate with LOPFI.
Jimmie Bell - second. Vote 5 — 0 all in favor. Carl then asked Tammy about the process and the
time it would take to complete. Tammy stated a fee of around $700.00 would have to be paid, a
request sent to LOPFI in April and City Council approval. She was pretty certain it could be
finalized by years end. Jimmie Bell stated “I think this is good, no reason not to.” Carl wanted to
know if the board would be notified when the process is complete. Tammy responded. The board
members will be mailed a letter confirming the transfer.

No other discussion.

Motion to adjourn by Bill Clark motioned, second by Jimmie Bell. Meeting adjourned at 10:17 a.m. with
a vote of 5-0.

Council Meeting Minutes
July 20, 2020

In response to the 2020 COVID-19 Pandemic and restrictions placed on
social distancing by the Centers for Disease Control, the City of Cabot
moved the monthly Council Meeting to the Veterans Park Event Center, 508
N. Lincoln, as advertised. This allowed for spacing between chairs, as
suggested. The meeting was both open to the public and an online meeting
with video through the web-based video conferencing tool Zoom. The event

Fire Pension Board Meeting
Feb/18/2020

A Fire Pension Board Meeting was held on Tuesday, February 18, 2020 at 10:00 a.m. in the conference
room at City Hall. Members present were: Carl Pickard, Jimmie Bell, and William (Bill) Clark. All others
were absent. Others present were: Mayor, Ken Kincade, City Attorney, Ben Hooper, City Clerk &
Treasurer, Tammy Yocom and Deputy Clerk, Lisa Milam.

1. Mayor, Ken Kincade called the meeting to order at 10:03.

Handouts were as follows, a copy of the Memo on Consolidation of Local Plan for year 2020 from the
Arkansas Fire & Police Pension Review Board, a voting ballet and an information update form to all
present.

2. Discussion regarding voting on board member’s ensued. Followed with a vote by ballot from all
present board members, the Mayor and Tammy. The vote was unanimous for all 5 members
residing within the state of Arkansas to serve on the board. Vote 5 — 0 in favor.

3. Discussion regarding voting on a 3% raise for 2020 retroactive to 1/01/2020. Motion to adopt, by
Jimmie Bell. Second by Carl Pickard. Vote 5 — 0 all in favor.

4. Discussion regarding consolidation with LOPFI. Carl Pickard asked about the amount of monies in
the Fire Pension Fund at present. Tammy handed out a Stephen’s statement confirming the
account balance as $3,018, 065.92 in the Fire Pension Relief Fund as of Dec. 31, 2019. Carl stated
that “The board has so few members now that it is hard to even get a quorum together, so if it is
all the same | feel like we should consolidate.” Carl then: motioned to consolidate with LOPFI.
Jimmie Bell - second. Vote 5 — 0 all in favor. Carl then asked Tammy about the process and the
time it would take to complete. Tammy stated a fee of around $700.00 would have to be paid, a
request sent to LOPFI in April and City Council approval. She was pretty certain it could be
finalized by years end. Jimmie Bell stated “I think this is good, no reason not to.” Carl wanted to
know if the board would be notified when the process is complete. Tammy responded. The board
members will be mailed a letter confirming the transfer.

No other discussion.

Motion to adjourn by Bill Clark motioned, second by Jimmie Bell. Meeting adjourned at 10:17 a.m. with
a vote of 5-0.

Moudy, City Attorney Ben Hooper and Garver – City Planner Kevin
Gambrill. Also in attendance, in person, were Chairman Young, and
absent were Claude Irvin and Mitch Ward.

A RESOLUTION EXPRESSING THE WILLINGNESS OF THE CITY OF CABOT,
ARKANSAS TO UTILIZE FEDERAL-AID SURFACE TRANSPORTATION
PROGRAM FUNDS; AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES

Program funds are available at 80% federal participation and 20% local cash match for the Main
Street Streetscape Phase III Project:

ARKANSAS THAT:

SECTION 1: The City of Cabot will participate in accordance with its designated
responsibility, including maintenance of this project.

SECTION 2: The Mayor and the City Clerk/Treasurer are hereby authorized to execute
all appropriate agreements and contracts necessary to expedite the construction of the above
stated improvement.

SECTION 3: The City Council pledges its full support and hereby authorizes the
Arkansas State Highway and Transportation Department to initiate action to implement this
project.

its passage.

Special Council Meeting Minutes
August 3, 2020

In response to the 2020 COVID-19 Pandemic and restrictions placed on
social distancing by the Centers for Disease Control, the City of Cabot
moved the monthly Council Meeting to the Veterans Park Event Center, 508
N. Lincoln, as advertised. This allowed for spacing between chairs, as
suggested. The meeting was both open to the public and an online meeting
with video through the web-based video conferencing tool Zoom. The event
was successfully streamed through YouTube.

Mayor Ken Kincade called to order the Special meeting of the Cabot City
Council at 6:47 p.m. on August 3, 2020 in the Veterans Park Event Center.
This meeting followed the regularly scheduled Work Session. Mayor Kincade
opened with prayer and led the Pledge of Allegiance.

Roll Call

A roll call was conducted. The following Council Members were present:
Ronald Waymack and Doug Warner attended the meeting in person and
also by Zoom. Council Members Norma Naquin, James Reid, Matt Webber,
Kevin Davis, Damon Bivins and Ed Long all attended the meeting via Zoom
only. Also in attendance were City Attorney Ben Hooper (by Zoom), City
Clerk & Treasurer Tammy Yocom, and HR Director Matthew Hood. Several
members of the public were also in attendance.

City Council
OLD BUSINESS: None

NEW BUSINESS: RESOLUTION NO. 28 OF 2020 — A RESOLUTION EXPRESSING
THE WILLINGNESS OF THE CITY OF CABOT, ARKANSAS TO UTILIZE FEDERAL-
AID SURFACE TRANSPORTATION PROGRAM FUNDS; AND FOR OTHER
PURPOSES was read by City Clerk & Treasurer Tammy Yocom. Mayor Kincade
explained this project would take Streetscape to the overpass with an estimated
project budget of $1,235,000 and an 80/20 grant match. This is necessary to get
Metroplan to consider the project. Motion to adopt by Mr. Long, second by Mr.
Reid. Motion passed unanimously by a Roll Call Vote.

services. She announced two companies bid and she is working through their references.

Cabot Parks and Recreation Commission Meeting
July 21, 2020 at 6:30pm
Veterans Park Community Center
508 North Lincoln, Cabot, Arkansas 72023

I.

Call to Order/Roll Call
Maggie Cope called the meeting to order at 6:30 pm.
Present: Maggie Cope, Greg Sled, Nick Whitaker, Tricia Ambeau, John Rudd,
John C. Thompson
Special Guest: Greg Crumpton

II.

Minutes of Regular Meeting
Minutes from the meeting held on June 16, 2020 were presented. JOHN C. THOMPSON
MOTIONED TO ACCEPT THE MINUTES OF JUNE 16, 2020, SECOND BY GREG SLED. ALL SAY AYE.

III.

Financials
General Director Travis presented the June 2020 financials. JOHN C. THOMPSON MOTIONED
TO ACCEPT THE JUNE 2020 FINACIALS AS PRESENTED, SECOND BY GREG SLED. Cabot Parks and
Recreation is generating half the amount of revenue. Most facilities are still running at half
capacity. Water Park should average about $30,000 per week in gate revenue. Current numbers
are between $15,000 and $17,000. Concession revenue is half. Departments have cut expenses
yielding the largest profit gain. Sustainability difficult as improvements and purchases will need
to be made. A $25,000 Pepsi bonus has been received. Rental refunds are still taking place;
however, rental reservations and deposits are picking back up. Sport refunds are completecontact has been made via email, phone. Correspondence regarding refunds has been tracked.
ALL SAY AYE IN PASSING THE JUNE 2020 FINANCIALS.
Programs
Programs Director Lorenzo Mendoza addresses the agenda for fall sports. Anticipates starting
registrations for baseball and softball. Spring sports uniforms and equipment has been
inventoried for potential future use. Programs staff has assisted daily with Aquatic Park
business and patron tracing. BMX- building is up. Garage door will go up on 7/22. Fence in front
of building will be redone for easier access. Adjustments to social distancing standards are
being made constantly. Doing well. Moved up to second in the state. Football- more questions
than answers. Possible push back to 8/1 for first day of registrations. Under current state
directive, football cannot be played. Individual drills can be done, but close contact play cannot
happen. Commissioner Whitaker asks if any plans/ policies have been made regarding refunds if

IV.

121

V.

the season does start, but is later cancelled- how to issue refunds, uniform orders, how to issue
refunds after uniforms have been ordered. Mr. Hilbert- football is a small organization, trying to
be more reactive than proactive. Affordability- uniform costs and registrations fees. Believes a
push back to Spring 2021 is best. A push back to August- leaves two weeks for practice, two
weeks for registration, season opener at the end of September. 7-week window of play
contingent on August push back. Spring play- field usage possible. Conversations for
associations that cannot play under state directive should happen quickly. Commissioner Rudd
inquires about dates if the state directive changes and close contact sports are allowed. Normal
cheer registrations would begin the last weekend of July. Minimum of 2-3 weeks for cheer
uniforms to arrive. Guarantee a preferred 10 games. Management, logistics and time restraints
discussed. Worries- lack of participants and volunteers. Conversations with Programs Director
are necessary regarding push backs/ spring season. Football board meeting scheduled for 7/22.
Flag Football board has decided to wait until green light is given for close contact sports. Unsure
of dates regarding uniform ordering-can use old jerseys. Board insurance questions.
Construction/Directors Report
General Director Travis Young provides update. Donita H. has retired after 14 years. The
Veterans Park Community Center is having A/C and humidity issues. In the process of getting it
fixed- working with a company that has the license to operate/ repair 40-50-ton A/C units.
Commercial Air has done adjustments to the thermostats. Therapy pool heater no longer works
after 14 years - 6-year normal lifespan. A new one has been ordered at $3200 and will be stored
as the therapy pool can only be utilized by one individual at a time. Has been ordered due to
the 6-8-week estimated delivery time out of California. As the directive changes regarding
persons and pool usage, the adjustment to the therapy pool heater will be made. A chlorinator
at the Aquatic Park stopped working- fixed with parts from therapy pool were used to fix it. A
mass communication text app system is in the works. Previously used Remind. Contract is in
review. Will be used to promote and market- should start around 8/1. Bridge repairs to the
Community Pond have been done- maintenance has been directed to a group out of NLR,
Peeples Lumber Supply for guaranteed for life treated lumber. As of 7/21, all disc golf tees have
been moved. Concrete tee pads are in place. Richie Road walking trail has been resealed as a
part of the grant funding. Riprap to walking trail bank to be completed. Renew Church has
volunteered to assist with cleanup and bank stabilization. City of Cabot assisted with bank
stabilization. Allman/Bevis- turf wrinkles have been taken care of. Nothing major at 321. Dirt
has been removed from Allman/ Bevis. Two dirt piles remain at 321. Aquatic Punch Cards-

122

concerns have been brought up regarding usage. Aquatic Park final day to be determined.
Working with Building Bridges on a walk-through fundraiser in Richie Rd. Park. Mike Wheeler
from the City of Cabot present. Asphalt/ shingle roof replaced. Membrane and flat roof
replacement supposed to be done at the Community City. Metal roofs at multiple Parks and
Recreation facilities need to be replaced. Pricing ranges from $30,000- $225,000. The City can
put everything under one contractor or individual bids can take place. City Attorney requests a
vote/ motion by Commission indicating that the City can act on behalf of Parks regarding the
insurance and roof replacement. City cannot put out bid until on Parks on agenda. JOHN C.
THOMPSON MOTIONED TO AMENDA JULY 21, 2020, AGENDA TO INCLUDE ROOF BID
DISCUSSION, SECOND BY GRED SLED. ALL SAY AYE. JOHN RUDD MOTIONED TO ALLOW THE
CITY TO BID OUT CABOT PARKS AND RECREATION FACILITY ROOFS. SECOND BY GREG SLED.
10 plus facilities. Estimated costs- $600,000-$700,000. Holding a check for $80,000 to complete
Community Center roof. ALL SAY AYE.
VI.

Old Business
IT and HR. Email shared at June’s Commission meeting from Cabot Mayor indicated that the IT
and HR department at the City would no longer be accessible to Cabot Parks and Recreation.
Commission decided to have Chairman Cope email the Mayor following said meeting. Waited
for three weeks for a response- received none before a follow up was sent. City Council
members responded to the follow up email, as did the Mayor. The email indicated that City
Attorney Ben Hooper and CPR Attorney Greg Crumpton made the decision. The City Attorney
informed CPR Attorney on the decision- no negotiation or feedback. CPR Attorney indicates
that we can handle HR until December. Budget for 2021 can include HR. CPR General Director
Young had a meeting with CPR staff regarding sexual harassment, discrimination, and social
media policies. Chain of command was discussed. Memorandum completed by CPR General
Director Young and signed by all attending staff at meeting. CPR compliance- during the interim
time, any HR related issue regarding the General Director will go straight to Chairman Cope in
lieu of Attorney Crumpton. Hiring an HR person to be determined. IT- defer to school district.

VII.

New Business
Youth Sports- Fall registration will open for baseball and softball. Per Arkansas Department of
Health certain items need to be addressed- guidelines on masks, gate fees, number of people
allowed in park per team. Additional sport option. Concerns brought forth- game schedules

123

must be sent to the Arkansas Department of Health. Employees handling gate feesdiscouraged. Fall registration- cheaper registration fees. How to obtain gate fees- Upfront at
time of registration or at each game? $15 extra added to registration to cover gate. Guarantee
8 games. Take out costs of gate workers. Breakeven point as of 2019 was $25/ person.
Limitations on passes? 40 people/ team at gate. Option to play on all nine fields in Cabot. Fire
code- 352 people/ side. Teams must leave the park after each game before next team is
allowed in. No vote necessary. General Director Young to reach out to Department of Health for
suggestion on best practices regarding gate.
VIII.

Community Input
John Rudd requests from General Director Young an elaboration on the City Council meeting
regarding a grant designed for Parks and Recreation. The grant concludes that the city is
essential. Cabot did pass- indicates that the city is open for business. Unsure of how it will
affect Parks and Recreation. Not designated funds- the purpose of the grant is to back fund
Covid-19 expenses. Cabot Parks and Recreation is tracking expenses related to Covid-19.
Current estimated costs- $1600. More to be labeled- items prior to June. Request by
Commissioner Whitaker to include Safe Room policies in August agenda.

IX.

Adjournment

July 21, 2020

***THIS WAS A ZOOM MEETING***
PRESENT: Candace Tomboli, Norma Naquin, Ed Long, Jay Lallu and Greg Jones
GUESTS PRESENT: Travis Young with Parks & Rec., Clint McGue, legal counsel, Amy Williams, Gina Jones, Gina Quattlebaum, all

Jay Lallu called the meeting to order at 8:37 a.m.

Funding Recaps – Cabot Foundation for Arts and Culture – Both John Rudd and Rebecca Williams were on the zoom meeting.
John talked about their mural that was completed in a week. He said that the mural was completed to promote tourism. He said that

about and John Rudd said that they got the numbers from Facebook.
Chamber Report – Amy Williams mentioned that our office had remained open through this pandemic, trying to continue to
promote Cabot and help our businesses. We are still planning Cabotfest and hoping to have it. It will look different for sure. Gina
Quattlebaum mentioned that we are planning our new teacher luncheon for this Thursday. We have some great goodie bags for
them donated by local businesses. We are getting some new Chamber software that will really enhance our website and provide a
lot of benefits for our members. Our website will look a lot more professional. Hopefully, next month we will hopefully have
something to look at on our community branding. We hope to bring all the logos together.
Cabot Parks & Rec – Travis Young was here and said that it was business as usual for them. This weekend Cabot will host the

our ball tournaments. We have several restrictions that is keeping people safe. For the year, he said that they are still currently
about $100,000 down. The aquatic park is only able to run at half capacity, which is hurting us some. We will not know the true
devastation of this pandemic until we get to probably September and October. We will discuss fall sports tonight at our parks and
rec. commission meeting. Currently in AR, we can play baseball and softball. We also have some BMX racing going on. We are
looking at possibly adding some running programs or something and we are trying to stay ahead of things and are making sure that
we have programs for our community and those around us.

back and forth last month, I think it all ended up going off without a hitch. The enforcement portion has been an issue over the past
year. I think that our code enforcement in Cabot really stepped this time and helped. Do we still need to wait another month before

12.

Quarterly Reports
Not less often than quarterly, the President/CEO of the Chamber shall submit reports to the
Mayor and City Council. Each report shall include a statement of the specific criteria
contained in numbered paragraph 5 of this contract and an articulation of compliance as to
each of those criteria. Each report shall also detail other actions the Chamber has taken to

13.

Comprehensive Financial Statements
The Chamber shall provide a comprehensive statement of financial review to the City for
all Economic Development Services activity provided under this Agreement at the City’s
request.

14.

Recapture Provision
Annually, the Chamber shall provide to the Mayor and to the Cabot City Council a written
financial accounting of the use of the moneys provided to the Chamber pursuant to this
Agreement, together with supporting documentation generally conforming to Arkansas
Legislative Audit's requirements and detailing the Chamber’s progress toward, or
achievement of, the specific criteria described herein. To the extent that criteria are not
satisfied on an annual basis, the Cabot City Council may, by adoption of a Resolution,
formally demand the refunding of the moneys previously transferred to the Chamber upon
the Cabot City Council’s decision that the reporting was insufficient and without merit or
that the agreed upon progress or criteria has not been achieved in a timely manner.

15.

Financial Accounts for Economic Development
All funding provided by the City pursuant to this Agreement will be used for Economic
Development Services as detailed herein. A separate bank account will be created by the
Chamber for the receipt and disbursement of such funds. All debits and credits to such
account will be strictly for Economic Development Services as described in this
Agreement.

16.

Non-Appropriation
The Chamber recognizes that the funding provided for in this Agreement is contingent
upon the appropriation of public funds by the Cabot City Council. Any money transferred
to the Chamber is restricted as to each item listed in any associated appropriation, and there
will be a credit to the City’s next year's budget for this Agreement for any money not spent.
In the event the Chamber’s President/CEO position is vacated, the portion of the budget
allocated for the payment of the salary for such position (or the portion of such salary
attributable to economic development duties) shall be returned to the City for each month
that the position is vacant. When the position is filled, the City shall resume the allocations
for such salary to the Chamber.

17.

Multiple Originals
The parties agree that the original and any executed copies of this Agreement shall serve
as originals of the Agreement for any evidentiary purposes in any court, administrative, or
other adversarial hearing.

18.

Merger
The parties agree that this Agreement incorporates the full agreement of the parties, and no
other discussions, writings, comments, or oral, verbal, or electronic communications of any
nature whatsoever are to be considered a part of, a clarification of, or an interpretation tool
for, the terms set forth within the Agreement.

19.

Severability
The provisions of this Agreement are hereby declared to be severable and, if any of such
provisions shall for any reason be held illegal or invalid, such holding shall not affect the
validity of the remainder of this Agreement.
